$comment: THE machine-readable Flash plugin protocol contract — the single source of truth for version, deadlines, quotas, error strings, the capability registry and transport limits. Normativity order: this file > docs/plugin-protocol.md prose > any implementation. Swift asserts its constants equal this file (PluginProtocolParityTests); the Rust SDK asserts its transport limits against it (wire.rs) and pins the behaviour in its runtime tests and probe crate. Changing anything here is a protocol change: update the host, SDK, affected plugins, tests, and docs in the same commit (repo rule 7 — no compatibility shims, no version bump while Flash has no external users).

deadlines_ms.$comment: One deadline table. startup: initialize must be answered immediately (no warm-catalog wait; config [plugins] startup_timeout tunes it). query: per-keystroke evaluate. live: search (late replies dropped, non-fatal). hints: activation hint pull; it blocks the AX queue ahead of the prepared model, so it is a fixed latency ceiling. perform: all four kinds; a manifest commands[] entry timeout_ms overrides for that entry. ping: reply budget for the idle-liveness probe (sent only after idle_before_ping_ms of inbound silence with no request in flight; ONE miss tears down). shutdown_grace: stdin-close -> SIGTERM; +500ms -> SIGKILL.

host_to_plugin.initialize: request {protocol_version} -> {ok, protocol_version}; reply immediately, once ever; ok:false or a version mismatch is terminal (flush, exit 0)
host_to_plugin.event: notification {name, payload}; never replied; `core:poll:<name>` ticks a cadence registered through `poll` and bypasses `listen`; `core:status.observed` carries {segments: [name]}, the complete set of unique nonempty manifest `status` names of this plugin that a status surface shows (empty = none), sent once after initialize and again on every change
host_to_plugin.evaluate: request {query, scope, surface} -> {ok, answers}; CPU-only over pre-warmed state
host_to_plugin.search: request {query, scope} -> {ok, rows}; live sources only, may do real work
host_to_plugin.hints: request {bundle_id, pid, front_window_frame} -> {ok, targets, context_pid?}; always live
host_to_plugin.perform: request {kind: resolve|command|action|navigate, ...} -> {ok, target_pid?, navigation_url?, message?} | {ok:false, unhandled:true} | {ok:false, error}

plugin_to_host_notifications.publish: {rows} — full-replacement catalog; host-owned store; empty rows = authoritative empty; transient failure = don't publish (host keeps last-good)
plugin_to_host_notifications.status: {segments: {name: value}} — manifest-declared names only; value is markup ("" clears) or a carousel object {prefix?: markup, lines: [markup], cycle_seconds: >= 1} the host rotates on its own clock (no lines clears; malformed objects are rejected whole)
plugin_to_host_notifications.poll: {registrations: {name: {every: seconds, priority} | {after: seconds, priority}}} — full-replacement set of the cadences (`every`) and one-shot deadlines (`after`, measured from receipt) the host should drive for this plugin; empty clears. Plugins must not arm their own timers or sleep to schedule work: the host folds every registration in the app onto one clock and sends `event {name: "core:poll:<name>"}` when one is due, regardless of manifest `listen`. A deadline fires once; repeating it unchanged in a later set neither re-arms nor re-fires it, and a changed or new name arms it afresh. Ticks are one-way and unacknowledged, so a plugin still running its previous callback drops the ones it missed instead of catching up. Bounds live in the `poll` section; a malformed or over-bound frame is rejected whole.
plugin_to_host_notifications.log: {level, message, fields, trace?} — content-free; trace names the interaction of the request being served

host_events.$comment: Every `core:*` event the host delivers through `event`, gated by manifest `listen` (plus capability for core:clipboard.changed). `replacement` kinds are state signals: each supersedes the earlier ones with the same coalescing key, the event name plus, for core:ax.changed, the payload pid and notification. While a replacement frame waits unsent in the host's outbound queue, a newer one with the same key drops it and joins the tail, so a child reads a subsequence of the emitted events in emission order; requests, responses and other events stay FIFO under the transport budget. Under backlog the plugin likewise keeps only the latest of each key. core:ax.changed (payload {pid, notification, bundle_id?}; both pid and a non-empty notification are required) reports one AX notification an observed app posted, one of `ax_notifications`: the value change of each keystroke is AXValueChanged, so match the notification instead of debouncing every change alike. core:network.changed (network interfaces, addresses, routes or DNS changed; payload {}) and core:volumes.changed (a volume mounted, unmounted or was renamed; payload {}) are payload-free, coalesced signals whose monitors run only while a plugin listens: re-read what you need.

poll.$comment: Bounds of a `poll` registration set. priority sets the slack the shared clock may add to a wake-up so unrelated ones coalesce (high 25 ms: a value on screen the user watches change; normal 100 ms: ordinary sampling and settles; low 1 s: background upkeep, remote pulls, retries). The core-only `system` priority is not available to plugins. every is floored at min_every_ms; every and after are capped at max_seconds; a set holds at most max_registrations names of 1..max_name_bytes characters from [a-z0-9_-].

row.$comment: Catalog row shape for publish and search. `source` is first-class and must name a manifest sources[].name; routing source_id stays host-stamped and never crosses the wire.

hint_target.$comment: The host revalidates geometry and target identity before clicking. context_id is an optional non-empty opaque string identifying the containing live source context; a changed context cancels the captured target. Omitted or null means unspecified.

effects.$comment: Closed union. copy_text/insert_text everywhere; open on rows only (answers cannot manufacture navigation). There is deliberately no run effect — argv side effects belong in perform, inside the sandbox.

quotas.$comment: Atomic rejection doctrine: any violation rejects the complete payload (a publish keeps the previous catalog; a reply serves empty); nothing is ever truncated.

errors.$comment: Canonical EXACT protocol-level error strings (spec-pinned; domain failures stay free-form and content-free). The response law: every result carries boolean `ok`; ok:false carries a non-empty `error` — except perform's {ok:false, unhandled:true} (not mine; host MAY fall back). A perform {ok:false, error} means mine-but-broke: the host MUST NOT fall back.
errors.protocol_mismatch: protocol version mismatch: host v<H>, plugin v1
errors.initialize_repeated: initialize may only be called once

id_semantics: positive monotonic integers per sender; host and plugin counters are independent and may overlap (an inbound id+method frame is always a request). Exactly one reply per id'd request. Responses to unknown ids are dropped silently. There is no cancellation: late replies are dropped and the deadline table is the contract.

trace.host_to_plugin: optional `trace` key on a request envelope (hints, search, evaluate, perform) naming the user interaction that caused it
trace.plugin_to_host: a `log` notification emitted while serving that request carries it back as params.trace; a malformed id is ignored

deadline.host_to_plugin: optional `deadline_ms` on a request envelope: the milliseconds the host still waits for the reply as it writes the request, a positive integer
deadline.plugin: a search or hints handler still running a tenth of the deadline (at most 50 ms) before it is dropped and answers errors.deadline_exceeded; evaluate and perform run to completion

encoding: UTF-8 JSON, one object per newline-terminated line both directions; geometry in NSScreen coordinates; undecodable or oversized lines are dropped (never fatal), the stream self-heals at the next newline; EOF discards an unterminated record before shutdown

transport_limits.$comment: Per-process admission bounds. Plugin replacement-event overflow retains one latest slot per coalescing key (host_events) in addition to the ordinary event backlog, at most plugin_replacement_slots keys at once; each slot obeys frame_bytes, and a new key beyond the bound is dropped like an overflowing ordinary event. A full synchronous control reply queue closes the transport rather than blocking the stdin reader.
